looks_like: Output follows input up and down; rheostat
Little output until a threshold, then steep rise
examples: Haemoglobin binding O2; glycogen phosphorylase cycle; Mos
source: MEK1 and ERK2 in oocyte extracts (the book's Table 5.1 lists 21)

looks_like: All-or-none, persists after input is removed
motifs: Positive or double-negative feedback with ultrasensitivity
examples: Oocyte maturation (Mos/ERK2); mitotic entry (Cdk1); cell fate decisions; memory in neural circuits

looks_like: Rises, then falls back under constant input
motifs: Negative feedback, incoherent feed-forward, state-dependent inactivation
examples: GPCRs; EGFR and Ras; bacterial chemotaxis

looks_like: All-or-none spikes at random times; input raises frequency, not amplitude
motifs: Fast positive plus slow negative feedback with noise
examples: Single ion channels (patch clamp); calcium signalling; Raf/ERK pulses

looks_like: Periodic output; input starts, stops or tunes them
motifs: Negative feedback with delay (Goodwin) or with a bistable trigger (relaxation)
examples: Calcium in some cells; sinoatrial node; embryonic cell cycle
